State Changev1DraftNot implemented

Slice: Complete Tool Maintenance

Step 4 of 5 in Keep tools in working order · after Tool Catalog — maintenance scheduled · before Tool Catalog — maintenance completed · State Change

Intent

Put a tool back in service once its maintenance is done. The shed manager looks at the Tool Maintenance screen, finds the tool whose work (sharpening, cleaning, tuning, and so on) is finished, and completes its maintenance. The tool leaves Tool Maintenance and returns to the Tool Catalog, available to borrow and hold again.

Completing records that the maintenance as a whole is done. It does not tick off tasks one by one: Tool Maintenance Scheduled carries the list of tasks, Tool Maintenance Tasks Changed carries the replacement list when the shed manager edits it, and Tool Maintenance Completed carries none. Completing closes every task together, whatever the list is at that moment.

What follows a completion is decided by the views that read Tool Maintenance Completed:

  • The tool's row leaves Tool Maintenance.
  • The tool is back on the Tool Catalog, available (Tool Catalog, as a continuation of its originating slice).

Trigger & Actor

The shed manager, from the Tool Maintenance screen, which offers Complete on every tool listed in it. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role (Amendment 6).

Command / Input

Command: Complete Tool Maintenance

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
toolIdToolIdyes—

A missing or malformed tool ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked (Amendment 7). The command carries no tasks, no notes and no date: the time is set by the system.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Maintenance @Shed Manager

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Maintenance Completed → context Tools

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
toolIdToolIdyesfrom command Complete Tool Maintenance
completedAtInstantyesassigned (set by the handler)

Read by: Tool Maintenance (the tool's row is removed) and Tool Catalog (the tool is back and available).

The event records neither who completed the maintenance nor which tasks were done. There is one shed manager role, and the model's event carries only the tool and the time.

Read Model / View

This slice has no read model in the model.

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Maintenance Completed removes the tool's row from Tool Maintenance and puts the tool back on the Tool Catalog. Each view is specified in its own doc (Tool Maintenance; Tool Catalog, whose "maintenance completed" position is a continuation with no doc of its own). Both are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

No invariants declared in the model.

  • INV-CTMN-1: Only the shed manager can complete a tool's maintenance.
    • Neighbors do not. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused with not-shed-manager.
    • A caller with no sign-in is refused with not-signed-in, before anything else is checked.
  • INV-CTMN-2: Completing maintenance for a tool that is not in maintenance records nothing new.
    • The request succeeds, so a double submit or a retry never fails and never records a second Tool Maintenance Completed. This covers a tool whose maintenance was already completed and a tool that was never sent for maintenance.
    • A tool is in maintenance from its Tool Maintenance Scheduled until the next Tool Maintenance Completed for it (or until it is retired, INV-CTMN-4).
  • INV-CTMN-3: The tool must exist.
  • INV-CTMN-4: A retired tool's maintenance cannot be completed.
    • A tool is retired once Tool Retired or Tool Lost is recorded for it. Retiring a tool in maintenance ends the maintenance (Tool Maintenance drops the row on Tool Retired), so there is nothing left to complete, and a retired tool must not return to the catalog.
    • The request is refused with tool-retired, the same reason Schedule Tool Maintenance gives for a retired tool. This holds even if the tool was in maintenance when it was retired.
  • INV-CTMN-5: Completing maintenance puts the tool back as it was before.
    • Only Tool Maintenance Completed is recorded. Nothing about the tool's loans or holds changes: a tool can only be scheduled while available with no holds, so none exist to be touched.
    • After completion the tool may be sent for maintenance again. The next Tool Maintenance Scheduled starts a new maintenance with its own tasks and time.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Happy path (INV-CTMN-5)

Given
  • the hedge trimmer was sent for maintenance to sharpen and clean it, and Tool Maintenance Scheduled is recorded for it
When
  • Complete Tool Maintenance: the shed manager completes the hedge trimmer's maintenance from Tool Maintenance
Then
  • Tool Maintenance Completed is recorded for the hedge trimmer, and nothing else.
  • Tool Maintenance no longer lists it, and Tool Catalog shows it available again.

Completed twice (INV-CTMN-2)

Given
  • Tool Maintenance Scheduled and then Tool Maintenance Completed are recorded for the hedge trimmer
When
  • Complete Tool Maintenance: the shed manager completes the hedge trimmer's maintenance again
Then
  • the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.

Tool never sent for maintenance (INV-CTMN-2)

Given
  • the ladder is in the shed and no maintenance was ever scheduled for it
When
  • Complete Tool Maintenance: the shed manager completes the ladder's maintenance
Then
  • the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.

Completed after the tasks were changed (INV-CTMN-5)

Given
  • the hedge trimmer was sent for maintenance to sharpen it, and Tool Maintenance Tasks Changed is recorded for it with the tasks "sharpen" and "replace the guard"
When
  • Complete Tool Maintenance: the shed manager completes the hedge trimmer's maintenance
Then
  • Tool Maintenance Completed is recorded for the hedge trimmer, and nothing else. It closes the tasks as last changed.

Sent for maintenance again after completing (INV-CTMN-5)

Given
  • the hedge trimmer's first maintenance was scheduled and completed
  • a second Tool Maintenance Scheduled is recorded for it with the task "oil the blade"
When
  • Complete Tool Maintenance: the shed manager completes the hedge trimmer's maintenance
Then
  • Tool Maintenance Completed is recorded for the hedge trimmer.

Tool retired while in maintenance (INV-CTMN-4)

Given
  • the hedge trimmer is in maintenance, and the shed manager then retires it (Tool Retired is recorded)
When
  • Complete Tool Maintenance: the shed manager completes the hedge trimmer's maintenance
Then
  • refused with tool-retired: "That tool has been retired." No event is recorded.

Tool recorded lost (INV-CTMN-4)

Given
  • Tool Lost is recorded for the cordless drill, which retired it
When
  • Complete Tool Maintenance: the shed manager completes the cordless drill's maintenance
Then
  • refused with tool-retired: "That tool has been retired." No event is recorded.

Unknown tool (INV-CTMN-3)

Given
  • no tool T9 has been added
When
  • Complete Tool Maintenance: the shed manager completes T9's maintenance
Then
  • refused with tool-not-found: "There is no such tool." No event is recorded.

Someone other than the shed manager (INV-CTMN-1)

Given
  • the hedge trimmer is in maintenance
When
  • Complete Tool Maintenance: a caller signed in without the shed-manager role asks to complete its maintenance
Then
  • refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can complete tool maintenance." No event is recorded, and the tool stays in maintenance.

No sign-in (INV-CTMN-1)

Given
  • the hedge trimmer is in maintenance
When
  • Complete Tool Maintenance: a caller with no sign-in asks to complete its maintenance
Then
  • refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the shed manager on the Tool Maintenance screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in, then not-shed-manager (INV-CTMN-1).
  2. tool-not-found (INV-CTMN-3).
  3. tool-retired (INV-CTMN-4).
  4. If the tool is not in maintenance, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-CTMN-2).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-CTMN-1
not-shed-managerOnly the shed manager can complete tool maintenance.INV-CTMN-1
tool-not-foundThere is no such tool.INV-CTMN-3
tool-retiredThat tool has been retired.INV-CTMN-4

not-signed-in, not-shed-manager, tool-not-found and tool-retired mean the same conditions as in the other shed-manager slices (Retire Tool, Schedule Tool Maintenance). tool-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen.

Idempotency: completing maintenance for a tool that is not in maintenance succeeds and records nothing (INV-CTMN-2).

Requests at the same moment: Complete Tool Maintenance is decided against the tool's events as already recorded, one at a time per tool. If Schedule Tool Maintenance or Retire Tool for the same tool is decided just before it, that stands and this command is decided against it; if just after, that slice decides against the completion.

There are no external calls in this slice, and no email is sent.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the shed manager may complete a tool's maintenance (INV-CTMN-1). Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role.
  • PII & compliance: none. Tool Maintenance Completed holds only the tool and a time.
  • Performance / SLA: none. Views are eventually consistent (constitution baseline).

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Maintenance Scheduled (Schedule Tool Maintenance): toolId. It starts a maintenance.
    • Tool Maintenance Tasks Changed (Schedule Tool Maintenance): toolId. It leaves the tool in maintenance, so it neither starts nor ends one and changes nothing in this slice's decision.
    • Tool Maintenance Completed (this slice): toolId. It ends one.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId. It ends a maintenance and retires the tool.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): toolId. A lost tool is retired by it.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Tool Maintenance (removes the row) and Tool Catalog (the tool returns, available).
  • Rules held in other docs: Check Out Tool and Place Hold must refuse a tool in maintenance, and Retire Tool must say that retiring a tool in maintenance ends it. Those are written in their own docs when they are revised; they are named here because they depend on this slice's event ending the maintenance. Tool Catalog's doc gains scenarios for the two maintenance events.

Open Questions

None.
